draft.rationale: The edit wraps the history-version creation in a try/catch whose added handler logs `Failed to create a history version for ${uid}` through strapi.log.error and then returns normally, so the caller that saved the entry is told nothing when the version was not recorded.

readLocalFiles adds `readdir(localExtensionsPath, ...).catch(() => {})` and then `if (!entries) return 0;`, so a directory that could not be read is reported as zero files read, which the caller cannot tell apart from an empty extensions folder.

parseDetails adds `} catch {}` around JSON.parse and then a second catch that logs `Failed to decrypt sync source details` and returns null, so a stored sync source that cannot be decrypted reads back as having no details.

The edit adds `} catch { return []; }` where attachment columns are collected from an audit's details, so a details row that cannot be parsed yields no attachment references and the audit is returned without its files.

The edit chains `.catch((e) => this.logger.error({ error: e, details: 'Error while sending form submission email', hookName }))` onto the mail send, so a failed form-submission email is only logged and the hook completes as if it had been delivered.

decryptPluginInput adds `} catch { return null; }` after decryptPropIfRequired, so a plugin input that cannot be decrypted becomes null and the plugin loads without its configuration instead of reporting the failure.
The migration's job() adds a catch that logs `Could not list failed jobs to scrub: ${e?.message}` and returns true, so a queue that cannot be read still marks the migration as completed.
The added catch logs `Failed to refresh ${this.service} access token` and returns `this.token`, the token the refresh just failed to renew, so the caller retries with an expired credential.
The edit replaces the document-lock lookup with a try that ends in `} catch { // swallow error }`, so a failure to read the lock is discarded and the global is returned with no lock status.

consumeOutboundMessages adds a catch that logs `[AgentChatBridge] Failed to clear task messages after a reply` and returns, so messages the reply already carried stay queued and the caller is not told they were not cleared.

resolveFileSecrets adds a catch that console.errors `Failed to read file for ${key} (${filePath})` and leaves `env[baseKey]` undefined, so the process boots with the secret unset while only the boot log records why.

The retention run adds `logger.error(error, \`Retention failed for collection ${task.collection}\`)` in its catch and moves on, so a collection whose rows could not be pruned is visible only in the log.

The provider listing adds a catch that logs `Skipping auth provider "${id}" when listing providers, as it could not be resolved` and returns null, so a broken provider silently disappears from the list callers use to offer sign-in.
The added catch logs `[Search] Cannot clean up after swapping in version ${activeVersion}` and continues, so the swap reports success while the previous index version is left behind.
The invitation send adds `.catch((e) => this.logger.error(e.message, e.stack))`, so a failed invitation email is logged and the invite call still returns its success message.
The added catch logs `Unable to schedule document update event` through Logger.error and returns, so a document that was never queued for update still looks persisted to the caller.

The membership check adds `try { const document = await Document.findByPk(model.id, ...); authorize(user, "read", document); return true; } catch (err) { return false; }`, so a failed document read or a permission error is answered as 'not this user', and the notification is skipped without the caller knowing why.
The webhook sync adds a catch that logs `[webhook] Failed to sync webhook for ${config.provider}: ${err}` and returns, so a deployment provider left with no webhook reports as configured.

The heartbeat write adds a catch that logs `Could not write the heartbeat of AI metadata job ${jobId}` with strapi.log.warn and returns, so a job whose heartbeat was never stored keeps its old `heartbeatAtMs` and another server can fail it as stale while it still runs.

The repository fetch adds a catch that logs `Failed to fetch repositories from Gitea` and returns [], so an unreachable or unauthorised Gitea integration shows an empty repository list instead of an error.

The added `} catch (_err) { return false; }` reports that the mentioned user cannot read the document whenever the access check itself failed, so a transient database error silently denies the share notification.

The session-store setup adds `redisClient.connect().catch((error) => { logger.error(`Failed to connect to Redis session store: ${error.message || error.code}`) })`, so a session store that never connects leaves the server booting normally with sessions that fail at request time.

The file comparison adds `const localStat = await fsStat(localPath).catch(() => {})` followed by `if (!localStat) return false;`, so a stat that failed for any reason is treated as the file being absent and the sync switches to uploading or removing it.

failInterruptedAIMetadataJobsOnListen adds a catch that logs `Could not fail the AI metadata jobs interrupted by a previous server`, so jobs left processing by the previous process keep that status and only the boot log records the failure.

The per-source loop adds `} catch (e) { this.logger.error(`Failed to backfill searchPath for source ${row.id}: ${e.message}`, e.stack); }` and the job still ends with `return true`, so sources that were never pinned to their default schema are reported as a completed migration.

The new class documents that `None of this is needed to deliver a message, so a refusal is logged and nothing is thrown`, and the added catch logs `Could not reach Meta to update a WhatsApp business profile.` with logger.warn; the file states the best-effort contract, so no caller loses a failure it needs.

resolveRichText adds a catch that console.errors once per config and returns null, and its own doc comment says `Returns null when a factory throws for these values: the field then loads without the extension`; the fallback is the documented contract of the function.

hasAllowedProtocol adds `} catch { return false; }` around `new URL(url)`: it is a parse-and-validate helper whose documented answer for a URL it cannot parse is false, so the failure is the expected result.

The edit adds `} catch { // Drivers that cannot read the setting keep the consecutive-id default. } return 1;` around a driver capability probe, so an unavailable setting falls back to the documented default.

The added catch warns `Cannot verify IP address due to invalid "IMPORT_IP_DENY_LIST" config` and returns true, which denies the request: a configuration failure falls back to the safe answer rather than to allowing traffic.
The added catch logs the failure, rolls the schema files back, and ends with `throw new errors.ApplicationError('Invalid schema edition')`, so the failure reaches the caller as a typed error.

The edit adds `.catch(() => null)` on the KV read and `.catch(() => undefined)` on the write, under the comment that a failing KV `never stops an app from connecting`: it is a cache the code refills, and the value it replaces is recomputed below.

The added catch logs `Failed to build the audit log payload for ${name}` and the save keeps a row without the transformer's fields; the file states audit logging is fail-open so an unawaited emitter cannot reject, and the audit log itself is the record, not the caller's outcome.

The added catch logs `Failed to generate types for ${boldArtifact}: ... Exiting` and calls returnWithMessage(), the CLI boundary that reports the failure and exits non-zero, so the failure is the program's visible outcome.

The edit adds `.catch((error) => { strapi.log.error(...) })` to a promise returned into onCommit that nobody awaits; the reason given in the comment is an unhandled rejection, which is the unawaited-promise shape and out of this policy's scope.

decryptKey adds `} catch { ... return null }` with a comment explaining that a value encrypted under a removed key is masked rather than failing the whole document read; the masked value is deliberate and the field is not used for authentication.

The edit replaces a silent `} catch { // Prevent unhandled rejections }` with a catch that logs `RPC "${method}" on "${channel}" failed`; a log added to a failure that was silent before improves the edit, so it does not notify, while the swallowed failure itself remains tracked debt.
The added `.catch((error: unknown) => { callback(errorFromUnknown(error)); })` passes the failure to the stream callback, so the write error reaches the consumer of the stream.

The added catch logs the low-level error with `logger.log(e)` and then throws `{ message: 'Error reading Airtable schema: received an unexpected response format from Airtable' }`, so the failure still reaches the import job as an error.
The added `} catch { throw new EnterpriseInstallError(`${REGISTRY_OPTION} is not a valid URL.`); }` converts the parse failure into a typed error the command reports, so nothing is hidden.

The added `} catch { NcError.get(context).badRequest(\`Invalid filterArrJson for bulk-aggregate bucket "${alias}"\`); }` converts a JSON parse failure into a client-visible bad-request error instead of returning a default.

The edit adds `try { return await Promise.race([timeout, subscription]); } catch { // Fall through to the retry below }` inside a retry loop that re-enters getSchema and finally rethrows, so the failure is retried and not discarded.
The added `} catch (_err) { throw AuthenticationError("Invalid token"); }` converts a decoding failure into an authentication error for the caller.
The added `catch { return false; }` sits inside a zod `.refine` predicate that answers whether a time zone is valid: false is the validation verdict, not a hidden failure.
The edit adds `settled.catch((error) => { failPending(error); })`, which routes a commit failure into the pending callbacks, so every attached callback receives the error.

The edit wraps applyPostbackRevenueVisibility in a try/catch whose body is `console.error("[sendPartnerPostback] Error applying revenue visibility", { ... })` followed by `return;`, so a failing revenue-visibility lookup ends the postback silently and the caller or the partner network cannot tell the send did not happen.

The new `try { await getGroupOrThrow({ programId, groupId }) } catch (error)` block does `if (error instanceof DubApiError) { return; }`, so a job whose group no longer exists finishes as a completed job and the missing group never reaches the job runner as a failure.

The catch-all was changed to `} catch { return null; }` and the function now answers a three-valued status, so an edge-config read failure returns the same inconclusive value as a domain that is simply not listed and the safety check reads as a clean domain.

The added catch bodies run `console.error("[screenRewardTooltipContradiction]", error); return { flagged: null };` and `return { suggestions: [] };`, so an evaluation that threw is indistinguishable from a review that found nothing.

The new try/catch around `redis.hset(\`${PARTNER_IDS_KEY_PREFIX}:${program.id}\`, ...)` only runs `console.error("Failed to map imported partner key", error, partner.key)` and continues, so an import whose partner-key mapping write failed reports every partner as imported while the mapping is missing.

The added catch runs `console.error(\`Error retallying payout ${payoutId}:\`, error)` and the loop moves on, so a payout whose amount could not be recomputed keeps its stale amount and the batch reports success.

The three added catches (`"[addMemberToStaging]"`, `"[updateMemberRoleInStaging]"`, `"[removeMemberFromStaging]"`) each `console.error` and `return;`, so a member sync that failed at the staging workspace reports as done.

The added catch around `prisma.commission.updateMany` only calls `await log({ message: \`[mockPayoutCompletion] Failed to mark commissions as paid ...\`, type: "errors" })` and continues to the next batch, so a partially marked payout completes as if every commission was paid.

The new `await Promise.allSettled([ qstash.publishJSON({ ... }) ... ])` around the remap jobs discards every rejection, so when the queue publish fails the partners were moved but no remap runs and the move still returns as successful.

`const results = await Promise.allSettled(partners.map((partner) => createPartner({ ... })))` is then reduced with `result.status === "fulfilled" && result.value ? [result.value] : []` and only the fulfilled ids are queued, so rejected partner creations disappear from an import that reports as finished.

The added `await Promise.allSettled([ bulkDeleteLinks(...), prisma.discoveredPartner.delete({ ... }) ])` drops the rejections of the link deletion and the enrollment deletion, so the invite is removed and reported deleted even when its links survived.

`await Promise.allSettled(user.projects.map(({ project }) => deleteWorkspaceAdmin(project)))` is chained with `.then(...)` that goes on to `prisma.user.delete(...)` without inspecting a single rejection, so a user is deleted while some of their workspaces survive.

The new attemptTokenRefresh ends in `} catch { return { valid: false, error: SESSION_EXPIRED } }`, and the outer catch falls back to the same helper, so a token verification that threw is answered as an ordinary expired session and the caller cannot tell an auth outage from a real expiry.

The catch that used to log was replaced with `} catch { // noop }`, and the code afterwards always redirects to the login route, so a logout whose request failed looks exactly like a completed logout.

The new addAssets takes `const results = await addAssetsToAlbum(...)`, counts only `results.filter(({ success }) => success).length` and shows `toastManager.success($t('assets_added_count', ...))`, so assets the server refused are reported to the user as added.

The new handleRemoveSharedLinkAssets loops `for (const result of results)` with `if (!result.success) { continue; }`, then toast the count of successful removals only, so a failed per-asset removal is silently dropped from a shared link that the user is told was updated.

The added handlePreload is `try { return await handleRequest(request); } catch (error) { console.error(\`Preload failed: ${error}\`); }`, so a failed preload resolves to undefined and the caller gets neither a response nor a failure.

The new migration wraps `await sql.raw(\`ALTER DATABASE "${databaseName}" RESET vchordrq.prewarm_dim;\`).execute(db)` in `try { ... } catch { logger.warn('Failed to reset vchordrq.prewarm_dim, skipping'); }`, so a migration that did not apply its change is recorded as applied.

The added catch around `await Promise.all(users.map((owner, i) => this.createOnThisDayMemories(...)))` only does `this.logger.error(\`Failed to create memories for ${target.toISO()}\`, error)` and the code still writes `lastOnThisDayDate: target.toISO()`, so the skipped day is never generated again.

The new block catches the reset of `updateAll(uniqueAssetIds, { duplicateId: null })` with `this.logger.error(\`Failed to remove duplicateId from assets: ${error.message}\`)` and returns the duplicate list unchanged, so assets stay flagged as duplicates while the caller sees a normal result.

The added `try { realpath = await this.storageRepository.realpath(originalPath); } catch { this.logger.warn('Unable to resolve realpath', { originalPath }); }` then calls `zip.addFile(realpath, filename)` with the unresolved path, so an archive entry whose real path failed is written under a path that may not exist.

The setup is wrapped in a new `try { ... } catch (error) { console.error("[ProxyStore] Failed to finish setup:", error) }` that lets the promise resolve, so a proxy store that never loaded its persisted settings is used with the in-memory defaults and callers cannot tell.

The new watcher wraps `this.teamCollectionService.changeTeamID(newWorkspace.teamID)` and `clearCollections()` in `catch (error) { console.error("Failed to sync team collections:", error) }`, so after a workspace switch the UI shows a workspace whose team collections belong to the previous one.

The new recordAdminImpersonationStarted ends in `} catch (error) { logger.warn("Admin audit: failed to record impersonation start", { error: ... }) }`, so an impersonation whose audit record was not written returns like a recorded one.

The added catch logs `Failed to delete logo for workspace ${workspace.id}. Continuing deletion.` and continues, so a workspace whose logo deletion failed is reported deleted while its storage object stays orphaned.
The new checkWorkers catch is `} catch { return; }` inside a 30-second watcher that only decides whether to log a warning, so the failure has no outcome beyond the next tick.

The added catch around `fs.rmdir(directory)` inspects `if (error.code !== 'ENOTEMPTY')` and only warns otherwise, which is the documented narrow catch of an expected filesystem error in a cleanup path.
The added line `this.complete.catch(() => {})` only suppresses the rejection warning of a promise nobody awaits, which the unawaited-promise clarification puts out of scope.
The added copy catch carries `// Not a JSON string` and falls through to the plain-text branch, which is the documented try-parse contract of reading an error response body.

The new fetchDomainConnectTemplateVersion is documented as a "Template version from the provider, or undefined when the lookup is inconclusive" and its catch is a bare `return;`, so absence is the stated contract.

The added catch logs `\`[getTremendousLogoUrl] Failed to read the content type of ${logo}\`` and then builds the `wsrv.nl` PNG fallback URL anyway, so the failure only changes which copy of a decorative logo is sent.

The added catch around getStripeRecipientPayoutMethod does `if (!pendingIdVerification) { throw error; }` before the warning, so the failure is rethrown whenever the identity-verification state does not explain it.

The added `} catch { // Continue to next URL if this one fails (timeout, SSRF guard, etc.)` is inside a loop that tries HEAD requests against candidate URLs and reports which one answered, so a failed candidate is an expected branch.

The edit deletes the old `logger.warn({ ... }, "Failed to get person segment IDs, returning empty array"); return [];` and instead does `if (error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError) { throw new DatabaseError(error.message); } throw error;`, so the silent empty result is replaced by a failure the caller must handle.

The new catch is documented directly above as "Fails open: this runs in the authenticated app layout, so a lookup error must cost the user a cosmetic support-chat label, never the whole page" and returns false, which is the stated contract.

The added serializeMessage returns null with the documented meaning "A message as JSON text, or null when JSON cannot hold it", and the new comparison treats null as "not equal" so the message is simply not de-duplicated.

The moved try/catch in the loader still does `logger.error("Unable to load OIDC public keys")` and returns `json({ error: "OIDC public keys unavailable" }, { status: 503 })`, a visible failure response at an HTTP boundary.
The edit only downgrades two existing `logger.error` calls to `logger.warn` and replaces a direct upsert with `syncAttioUser(payload, attioClient)`; no failure handling is added or removed.
The added catch starts with `if (!(error instanceof ConnectorError)) { throw error; }` and converts only connector errors into their code, so anything unexpected is rethrown.
The added catch body is `if (!(error instanceof SlonikError) && !(error instanceof DatabaseError)) { throw error; }` and maps only database errors, so unrelated failures still reach the caller.
The only change is renaming `signInAuditDatabaseHook` to `signInAuditPlugin` inside an existing comment; no code that handles a failure is touched.

The added catch converts the failure with `throw new Error(\`Invalid DATABASE_URL format: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'}\`)`, so the startup failure still reaches the process.
The added catch is `throw new Error(\`Failed to decode redis options: ${error}\`);`, which rethrows the failure with more context instead of hiding it.
The catch does `console.error(\`Unhandled plugin exception: ${error.message || error}\`); throw error;`, so the failure is both reported and rethrown to the host.

The added catch rethrows what it recognises with `if (error instanceof DubApiError || error instanceof z.ZodError) { throw error; }` and converts the rest into `throw new DubApiError({ code: "bad_request", ... })`, a typed failure the caller must handle.
